# Love Mail

## Overview
We are building a Next.js application for displaying ghost sightings across the United States. The name of the application is Wraithwatchers. This Is intended to be a fun, project that takes synthetic data about data ghost sightings and displays them on a map and table. It also allow s you to add new sightings

Love Mail is a thoughtful messaging app designed to strengthen communication between partners.
Whether it’s a sweet daily note, a shared to-do list, a shopping reminder, or a synced calendar event, Love Mail helps couples stay connected without stepping on each other’s schedules. Built for busy lives and meaningful relationships, the app encourages intentional communication and emotional support — making it easier to express love, coordinate tasks, and grow together.

Love Mail is a thoughtful messaging app that strengthens couple communication by enabling non-intrusive sharing of sweet notes, coordinated to-do lists, shopping reminders, and synced calendar events, supporting busy lives and intentional connection


##Initial Instructions
-I want you to play the role of expert full-stack developer.

-do not write any code just yet

##Functionality
-Refer to the mockups that I am supplying
-The basic functionality of the application is composed of three different pages.
-Page 1: Create love mail
--This page includes notes and sweet nothings, like good morning, my love! thinking of you.
--This page features an interactive calendar that displays all upcoming events for the current month.
Users can click on any date to add events or reminders — for example, “May 15: Movie Night” or “May 20: Anniversary Dinner.” Once added, reminders appear neatly beneath the calendar, making it easy to track important moments and shared plans.

--this page also includes a Shared tasks & list for example, grocery list: milk, eggs, bread, or like for example to-do: water plants, pick up your dry cleaning.


-Page 2:  Update Love Mail
--this page allows users to create new love mails. It provides an interface to include the various motes & sweet nothings, share task & lists and interactive calendar  to add events or reminders.

-Page 3: Confirmation Form
--This page appears after the user has entered an updated love mail.


##Visual Identity

	<Visual-identity>
					"Design a warm, inviting, and functionally elegant visual identity for the 'Love Mail' web application. The aesthetic should be clean and contemporary, infused with subtle romantic touches inspired by heartfelt letters and gentle connection.
					Key elements to incorporate:
					Color Palette: Utilize a soft, harmonious palette featuring muted pastel pinks, rose gold, creamy off-whites, a gentle lavender or light grey, and possibly a subtle, warm teal or sage green for accent. The goal is a comforting, soothing feel, avoiding harsh or overly vibrant tones.
					Iconography: Develop custom icons that are clean-lined and slightly whimsical. The core 'envelope with a heart' motif (similar to the provided samples, particularly the top right and bottom left) should be central. Other icons for notes, lists, and calendar events should be simple, intuitive, and carry a hint of this romantic, caring style.
					Typography: Select a friendly, highly legible sans-serif font for body text and a slightly more elegant, yet still clean, sans-serif or a very subtle script-like font for headings or special messages, conveying warmth and personal touch.
					Imagery/Illustrations: If illustrations are used, they should be simple, line-art based, or flat design, depicting concepts of connection, shared activities, or gentle reminders, all within the defined color palette.
					Overall Mood: The design should evoke a sense of calm, thoughtful communication, ease of use, and emotional support. It needs to feel personal and intimate, yet organized and efficient, reflecting the app's ability to help couples manage tasks and express love without stress."
	</visual-identity>

```diff
+ &#39;use client&#39;;
+ 
+ import { useState } from &#39;react&#39;;
+ 
+ interface CalendarEvent {
+   date: number;
+   title: string;
+   color: string;
+ }
+ 
+ interface CalendarProps {
+   events?: CalendarEvent[];
+   onDateClick?: (date: number) =&gt; void;
+ }
+ 
+ export default function Calendar({ events = [], onDateClick }: CalendarProps) {
+   const [currentDate] = useState(new Date());
+   const month = currentDate.getMonth();
+   const year = currentDate.getFullYear();
+   const monthName = currentDate.toLocaleString(&#39;default&#39;, { month: &#39;long&#39; });
+ 
+   // Get first day of month and number of days
+   const firstDay = new Date(year, month, 1).getDay();
+   const daysInMonth = new Date(year, month + 1, 0).getDate();
+ 
+   // Create array of days
+   const days = [];
+   // Empty cells for days before month starts
+   for (let i = 0; i &lt; firstDay; i++) {
+     days.push(null);
+   }
+   // Days of the month
+   for (let i = 1; i &lt;= daysInMonth; i++) {
+     days.push(i);
+   }
+ 
+   const getEventForDate = (date: number | null) =&gt; {
+     if (date === null) return null;
+     return events.find(e =&gt; e.date === date);
+   };
+ 
+   return (
+     &lt;div className=&quot;bg-white rounded-lg p-4 shadow-sm&quot;&gt;
+       &lt;h3 className=&quot;text-lg font-semibold text-[#5a5a5a] mb-4&quot;&gt;{monthName} {year}&lt;/h3&gt;
+       &lt;div className=&quot;grid grid-cols-7 gap-2&quot;&gt;
+         {[&#39;Sun&#39;, &#39;Mon&#39;, &#39;Tue&#39;, &#39;Wed&#39;, &#39;Thu&#39;, &#39;Fri&#39;, &#39;Sat&#39;].map(day =&gt; (
+           &lt;div key={day} className=&quot;text-center text-sm font-medium text-[#8a8a8a] py-2&quot;&gt;
+             {day}
+           &lt;/div&gt;
+         ))}
+         {days.map((day, index) =&gt; {
+           const event = getEventForDate(day);
+           return (
+             &lt;button
+               key={index}
+               onClick={() =&gt; day &amp;&amp; onDateClick?.(day)}
+               className={&#96;aspect-square rounded-lg text-sm transition-colors ${
+                 day
+                   ? event
+                     ? &#96;bg-[${event.color}] text-white hover:opacity-90&#96;
+                     : &#39;bg-gray-50 text-[#5a5a5a] hover:bg-[#f5d7d7]&#39;
+                   : &#39;&#39;
+               }&#96;}
+               disabled={!day}
+             &gt;
+               {day}
+             &lt;/button&gt;
+           );
+         })}
+       &lt;/div&gt;
+     &lt;/div&gt;
+   );
+ }
+ 
```

</details>
